title: Introduce tenant coverage shadow tables and join circuit breakers to reduce hot joins
creator: Riya Patel
description:
Background: Several control-plane read paths that power tenant dashboards and RBAC checks perform expensive multi-join scans against event_stream, project_assignments, and tenant_quota tables. Under load these joins produce 200-800ms tail latencies and frequent planner timeouts during spikes. We observed correlated incidents during the 2026-01 spike where bulk sync jobs amplified join cost.

Proposal: Create lightweight "tenant_coverage_shadow" tables that maintain a compact, per-tenant summary of the frequently-joined attributes (active_project_count, recent_event_cutoff, assignment_hash, quota_bucket). Populate shadow tables via an event-driven change-data-capture (CDC) stream from the primary tables and use them as the primary join target for latency-sensitive queries. Additionally, add a query-layer "join circuit breaker" that detects join cardinality blowups (based on pg_stats estimates or runtime row-count thresholds) and switches queries to a bounded approximation path using shadow tables + bloom-filter membership checks.

Goals: reduce 95/99 tail for dashboard and authorization reads by ~3-10x, eliminate planner timeouts for these endpoints, and provide a safe fallback with bounded correctness during rebuilds or CDC lag.
acceptance_criteria: 95th percentile read latency for tenant summary endpoint reduced by >=3x in production canary
No planner timeouts observed for the targeted queries in 7-day canary window
CDC-driven shadow tables show <5s median replication lag in dedicated region canary
Rollout can be toggled per-route via runtime flag and automatically falls back to original join on >1% error rate
migration_plan: 1) Add new tenant_coverage_shadow schema and create minimal columns (tenant_id PK, active_projects INT, recent_event_ts TIMESTAMP, assignment_hash TEXT, quota_bucket TEXT)
2) Backfill snapshot using batched copies (limit 10k tenants per batch) with VACUUM/ANALYZE between batches to keep planner stats current
3) Deploy CDC connector (published Kafka topic) that streams INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE from event_stream, project_assignments, tenant_quota into a transformer service
4) Transformer service applies idempotent upserts to shadow table using COPY/UPSERT and emits metrics for replication lag
5) Create CONCURRENTLY covering partial indexes on tenant_coverage_shadow (tenant_id), and on event_stream (tenant_id, event_type) using CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY
6) Switch a single non-critical read route to use shadow table behind a feature flag and observe metrics for 48h in canary
7) Gradually increase routes and tenants served, while monitoring correctness and latency
8) After successful canary, remove the most expensive join and leave shadow table in place as primary read path
rollout_plan: Canary on control-plane-prod region A: enable flag for 1% of tenants for 48h -> 10% for 72h -> 50% for 7d -> full. Automatic rollback if error_rate > 1% or 99th latency regresses >20% compared to baseline. Post-mortem gate after full rollout to confirm cost and correctness metrics.
risks_and_mitigations: CDC lag causing stale reads: mitigation - surface replication_lag metric and circuit-breaker to fallback to original join when lag > 30s
Shadow table bloat from churn: mitigation - periodic compaction job and retention policy; keep only recent_event_ts window and aggregate older data
Write amplification on high-velocity tenants: mitigation - batch upserts and rate-limit transformer writes per-tenant
Operational complexity: mitigation - provide runbook + alerting + dashboard; initial canary on low-traffic tenants
monitoring_and_metrics: Planner timeout and query cancellation counts
Join circuit-breaker activations and fallback rate
Database CPU and IO on primary tables vs shadow tables
tests: Unit tests for transformer idempotency (upsert, delete)
Integration tests for CDC pipeline using a local Postgres replica
Load test reproducing join-heavy workload in staging with synthetic tenant distribution
Chaos test: simulate shadow table outage and verify circuit-breaker fallback and correctness
comments: 2026-02-20 - Riya Patel: Initial spike completed. Confirmed top 5 queries responsible for 62% of join CPU on the control-plane primary DB. Prototype shadow schema reduces estimated join rows by ~95%.
2026-02-25 - Bennett Chu: Reviewed prototype and suggested adding assignment_hash (64-bit murmur) to enable cheap equality checks instead of full joins. Also suggested partial indexes on active flag.
2026-03-03 - SRE (Marcus Nguyen): Ran staging load test; observed replication lag spikes during backfill. Action: add batching throttle and schedule backfill during low-traffic windows.
